def _scope_learner_ksb_impact_payload(request, scope, identifier):
    scope = clean_str(scope) or 'programme'
    identifier = clean_str(identifier)
    lineage = scope_placement_lineage(scope, identifier)
    module_rows, week_rows, component_rows, mapping_rows = authoring_scope_data(scope, identifier)
    if not lineage.get('found') and not module_rows:
        return None, json_error(f'{scope.title()} not found.', status=404)
    mapping_rows = mappings_with_inferred_sources(mapping_rows, module_rows)
    required_ksbs = required_ksbs_for_request(request, module_rows, scope, identifier)
    coverage = annotate_coverage_sources(build_coverage(
        required_ksbs,
        mapping_rows,
        module_rows,
        week_rows,
        component_rows,
        include_mapping_only=not bool(required_ksbs),
    ))
    learner_status = clean_str(request.GET.get('learnerStatus') or request.GET.get('status'))
    learners = assigned_learners_for_scope(
        scope,
        identifier,
        '' if learner_status.lower() in {'', 'all'} else learner_status,
        lineage=lineage,
    )
    learner_ids = [
        int(row.get('sourceId') if row.get('sourceKind') == 'learner' else row.get('id'))
        for row in learners
        if str(row.get('sourceId') if row.get('sourceKind') == 'learner' else row.get('id')).isdigit()
    ]
    scope_codes = [item.get('code') for item in coverage.get('items', [])]
    component_ids = [clean_str(row.get('id')) for row in component_rows if clean_str(row.get('id'))]
    # What this scope authored, split by the group that delivers it, so every
    # denominator below is the weight and hours a single learner is assigned
    # rather than the scope's whole content.
    plan = scope_authored_plan(module_rows, component_rows, coverage.get('items', []))
    # Only the programme — the widest scope — may count an activity that carries
    # no component reference. Anywhere narrower that would be a guess about which
    # cohort or group the activity belonged to.
    include_unattributed = scope == 'programme'
    # The module progress screens (?moduleProgress=1) show only this scope's
    # activity, so other scopes' activity -- ~10k rows of a learner's programme
    # history for one module -- stays in the database and is only counted.
    # The Achievement panels list it under Activity, so they still read it.
    in_scope_only = request.GET.get('moduleProgress') == '1' and not include_unattributed
    progress_totals, progress_rows, excluded_progress_rows = learner_progress_ksb_consumption(
        learner_ids, scope_codes, component_ids, include_unattributed,
        restrict_to_components=not include_unattributed,
        scope=scope,
        scope_identifier=identifier,
        in_scope_only=in_scope_only,
    )
    out_of_scope_count = None
    if in_scope_only and learner_ids and connection.vendor == 'postgresql':
        try:
            out_of_scope_count = out_of_scope_progress_count(learner_ids, *progress_scope_predicate(
                {clean_str(value) for value in component_ids if clean_str(value)},
                PROGRESS_LINEAGE_COLUMN_BY_SCOPE.get(scope) or '', clean_str(identifier),
            ))
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning('Could not count out-of-scope progress: %s', exc)
    (
        reflection_declared_totals,
        reflection_rows,
        excluded_reflection_rows,
        unlinked_reflection_rows,
    ) = reflection_submission_ksb_consumption(
        learners, scope_codes, component_ids,
        restrict_to_components=not include_unattributed,
        include_unattributed=include_unattributed,
    )
    evidence_by_progress = progress_evidence_index(
        [row.get('progressId') for row in progress_rows]
        + [row.get('progressId') for row in excluded_progress_rows]
        + [row.get('progressEntryId') for row in reflection_rows]
        + [row.get('progressEntryId') for row in excluded_reflection_rows]
    )
    activities = learner_activity_trace(
        progress_rows,
        excluded_progress_rows,
        reflection_rows,
        excluded_reflection_rows,
        evidence_by_progress,
    )
    learners = apply_reflection_otjh_to_learners(learners, reflection_rows)
    learner_plans = learner_plans_for_scope(plan, learners)
    # One row per learner per component of their plan: 293k rows / ~220 MB for
    # a single group of 34 learners, and only the module progress screens read
    # it (learner_activity_status / module_progress_metrics, ?moduleProgress=1).
    # Every other caller -- the scope Achievement panels -- never looks at it.
    include_activity_plan = request.GET.get('moduleProgress') == '1'
    activity_plan = learner_activity_plan(
        learners, component_rows, module_rows, week_rows, activities, plan, learner_plans,
    ) if include_activity_plan else None
    learner_consumption = learner_consumption_payload(
        learners,
        coverage.get('items', []),
        progress_totals,
        reflection_declared_totals,
        expected_by_learner={
            learner_id: entry.get('ksbWeights') or {}
            for learner_id, entry in learner_plans.items()
        },
    )
    out_of_scope_progress = [
        row for row in excluded_progress_rows
        if row.get('scopeStatus') in {'out_of_scope', 'unattributed'}
    ]
    excluded_progress_rows = [
        row for row in excluded_progress_rows
        if row.get('scopeStatus') not in {'out_of_scope', 'unattributed'}
    ]
    otjh = scope_otjh_summary(plan, learner_plans, learners, activities)
    ksb = scope_ksb_achievement(
        coverage.get('items', []), learner_consumption, learners, plan, learner_plans,
    )
    payload = {
        'scope': scope,
        'identifier': identifier,
        'lineage': lineage,
        'placementBasis': lineage.get('placementBasis'),
        'structure': {
            'moduleCount': len(module_rows),
            'weekCount': len(week_rows),
            'componentCount': len(component_rows),
            'ksbMappingCount': len(mapping_rows),
            # How many distinct groups deliver this scope. Above one, the scope's
            # authored totals and its per-learner totals are different figures.
            'groupCount': len({key for key in plan.get('groupKeys', set()) if key}),
        },
        'assignedLearnerCount': len(learners),
        'assignedLearners': learners,
        # `programmeCoverage` was a second copy of this same payload; nothing
        # reads it any more (the programme card uses ?view=summary).
        'coverage': coverage,
        # The two roll-ups this whole read exists for: hours actually done, and
        # KSB weight actually earned, for this scope and no other.
        'otjhAchievement': otjh,
        'ksbAchievement': ksb,
        'learnerKsbConsumption': learner_consumption,
        'learnerActivities': activities,
        'learnerActivityCount': len(activities),
        **({
            'learnerActivityPlan': activity_plan,
            'learnerActivityPlanCount': len(activity_plan),
        } if include_activity_plan else {}),
        'ksbAchievementPolicy': {
            'achievedWeightSource': 'learner_progress_ksbs',
            'reflectionKsbRole': 'supplementary_evidence',
            'reflectionKsbCountsTowardAchievedWeight': False,
            'reflectionLearnerResolution': 'progress_entry_id',
            'expectedOtjhSource': 'learner_progress_entries|curriculum_component',
            'actualOtjhSource': 'learning_reflection_submissions',
            'scopeAttribution': 'curriculum.components.id',
            'unattributedActivityCounts': include_unattributed,
            # A learner is measured against the modules of the group enrolment
            # placed them in, not against every module in the scope.
            'expectedWeightBasis': 'learner_group',
            'plannedOtjhBasis': 'learner_group',
        },
        'consumptionSources': {
            'progress': progress_rows,
            'learningReflectionSubmissions': reflection_rows,
            'excludedProgress': excluded_progress_rows,
            'excludedLearningReflectionSubmissions': excluded_reflection_rows,
            'unlinkedLearningReflectionSubmissions': unlinked_reflection_rows,
            # Achieved activity that belongs to a different scope inside the same
            # programme -- the gap between this scope's total and the learner's
            # programme total. Sent as a count: the rows were 8-11 MB of a
            # module or cohort response and the page only ever showed how many.
            'outOfScopeProgressCount': len(out_of_scope_progress) if out_of_scope_count is None else out_of_scope_count,
            'evidenceByProgressEntry': evidence_by_progress,
        },
    }
    return payload, None

def _scope_learner_roster_payload_uncached(request, scope, identifier):
    """Who enrolment placed inside a curriculum scope, and how they split up.

    Curriculum never writes learner placements: ``Learner.learners`` is owned by
    enrolment and read here so each level of the hierarchy can show who is
    arriving. A module/week/component has no roster of its own — the learners who
    meet it are the ones placed in the group that delivers it, which is what
    ``placementBasis`` says out loud.
    """
    scope = clean_str(scope) or 'programme'
    identifier = clean_str(identifier)
    lineage = scope_placement_lineage(scope, identifier)
    learner_status = clean_str(request.GET.get('learnerStatus') or request.GET.get('status'))
    learners = assigned_learners_for_scope(
        scope,
        identifier,
        '' if learner_status.lower() in {'', 'all'} else learner_status,
        lineage=lineage,
    )
    cohort_filter = normalise(clean_str(request.GET.get('cohort')))
    group_filter = normalise(clean_str(request.GET.get('group')))
    if cohort_filter:
        learners = [row for row in learners if normalise(row.get('cohort')) == cohort_filter]
    if group_filter:
        learners = [row for row in learners if normalise(row.get('group')) == group_filter]

    by_cohort = Counter()
    by_group = Counter()
    for row in learners:
        cohort_name = clean_str(row.get('cohort'))
        group_name = clean_str(row.get('group'))
        if cohort_name:
            by_cohort[cohort_name] += 1
        if cohort_name and group_name:
            by_group[f'{cohort_name}||{group_name}'] += 1

    # Bulk Attendance only needs the placement identity to intersect this
    # roster with the KBC directory. Avoid serialising hours, coaching and
    # progress fields for that screen; the compact projection keeps the same
    # endpoint contract for every other caller while making its response much
    # smaller over the remote database connection.
    compact = truthy(request.GET.get('compact'))
    assigned_learners = learners
    if compact:
        assigned_learners = [
            {
                'id': row.get('id'),
                'name': row.get('name') or '',
                'email': row.get('email') or '',
                'cohort': row.get('cohort') or '',
                'group': row.get('group') or '',
                'cohortId': row.get('cohortId') or '',
                'groupId': row.get('groupId') or '',
            }
            for row in learners
        ]

    return {
        'scope': scope,
        'identifier': identifier,
        'lineage': lineage,
        'placementBasis': lineage.get('placementBasis'),
        # Placements are made by enrolment; curriculum only reads them.
        'source': 'enrolment',
        'editable': False,
        'assignedLearnerCount': len(learners),
        'assignedLearners': assigned_learners,
        'countsByCohort': dict(by_cohort),
        'countsByGroup': dict(by_group),
    }

def programme_achievement_inputs_uncached(request, programme_id):
    """Read actual consumption without building the general-purpose impact report.

    Keep the same scope, placement, source and canonical progress readers as
    impact. Reflections, evidence, OTJH and the learner-by-component activity
    plan are not inputs to the Achievement tables and must not be built here.
    """
    from .ksb_achievement import achievement_definitions

    programme_id = clean_str(programme_id)
    with curriculum_read_scope(targeted_child_reads=True):
        lineage = scope_placement_lineage('programme', programme_id)
        modules, _weeks, components, mappings = authoring_scope_data('programme', programme_id)
        if not lineage.get('found') and not modules:
            return None, json_error('Programme not found.', status=404)
        mappings = mappings_with_inferred_sources(mappings, modules)
        required = required_ksbs_for_request(request, modules, 'programme', programme_id)
        definitions = achievement_definitions(required, mappings)
        learner_status = clean_str(request.GET.get('learnerStatus') or request.GET.get('status'))
        learners = assigned_learners_for_scope(
            'programme', programme_id,
            '' if learner_status.lower() in {'', 'all'} else learner_status,
            lineage=lineage,
        )
        learner_ids = [
            int(row.get('sourceId') if row.get('sourceKind') == 'learner' else row.get('id'))
            for row in learners
            if str(row.get('sourceId') if row.get('sourceKind') == 'learner' else row.get('id')).isdigit()
        ]
        _totals, progress, _excluded = learner_progress_ksb_consumption(
            learner_ids, [item.get('code') for item in definitions],
            [clean_str(row.get('id')) for row in components if clean_str(row.get('id'))],
            True, restrict_to_components=False, scope='programme', scope_identifier=programme_id,
            # Achievement keeps only rows whose code is an applied definition,
            # and only achieved, in-scope ones (see _achievement_projection).
            codes_only=True, achievement_rows_only=True,
        )
        return {
            'coverage': {'items': definitions},
            'assignedLearners': learners,
            'consumptionSources': {'progress': progress},
        }, None

def resolve_coverage_source(request, module_rows, scope='', identifier=''):
    """(source_type, source_id, origin) for a coverage request.

    `origin` names where the answer came from -- 'request', 'programme',
    'module', 'programme-name', or 'all-profiles' when nothing identified one
    and the union of every active profile stands in as the required set. It is
    reported on the response so a page can say which source it is showing
    instead of quietly listing KSBs from everywhere.
    """
    source_type, source_id = split_ksb_source(
        request.GET.get('source_type') or request.GET.get('sourceType') or '',
        request.GET.get('source_id') or request.GET.get('sourceId') or '',
    )
    if source_type or source_id:
        return source_type, source_id, 'request'
    if not scope:
        return '', '', 'all-profiles'
    source_type, source_id, origin = infer_source_from_scope(module_rows, scope, identifier)
    if not source_type or not source_id:
        return '', '', 'all-profiles'
    return source_type, source_id, origin

def scope_learner_roster_entry(request, scope, identifier):
    """The encoded roster response, keyed by scope and every narrowing filter.

    The 30s TTL stays exactly as it was, deliberately. Placements are written
    by enrolment and the hours on each row by learner/hours code, and neither
    bumps the curriculum epoch, so the TTL is the only thing bounding how stale
    this can be. Caching the encoded form changes how a hit is served (no
    re-serialisation, 304 when unchanged), not when the data is re-read.
    """
    scope = clean_str(scope) or 'programme'
    identifier = clean_str(identifier)
    learner_status = clean_str(request.GET.get('learnerStatus') or request.GET.get('status')).lower()
    cohort = normalise(clean_str(request.GET.get('cohort')))
    group = normalise(clean_str(request.GET.get('group')))
    compact = '1' if truthy(request.GET.get('compact')) else '0'
    key = f'learner-roster-response:{scope}:{identifier}:{learner_status}:{cohort}:{group}:{compact}'
    return cached_curriculum_value(
        key,
        lambda: encode_json_entry(_scope_learner_roster_payload_uncached(request, scope, identifier)),
        ttl=30,
        scope=identifier if scope == 'programme' else None,
    )

def coverage_entry(request, scope='', identifier=''):
    """The encoded coverage response for a scope, from the epoch-aware cache.

    Coverage is read-only and rebuilt from authoring rows, so caching it
    prevents simultaneous programme-page requests from each scanning the same
    modules, weeks, components and mappings. What is cached is the encoded
    response (http_cache): the JSON exactly as the view produced it, its gzip
    form and an ETag. An error response is cached with its status, as before.

    TTL: still 60s, deliberately. Most of what this reads is written only
    through curriculum handlers, which bump the shared epoch and retire the
    entry at once (modules, weeks, components, KSB mappings, programme configs,
    KSB profiles). The exception is the Skills England requirement list: it is
    read straight from standard_ksbs at build time, and that table changes by
    manual SQL import, which bumps nothing. The 60s expiry is what bounds how
    long coverage can lag such an import, so it stays until the import path
    invalidates the curriculum cache itself.
    """
    # Read exactly as _coverage_response_uncached() reads them, so a key can
    # never name a different source from the one its document was built for.
    source_type = clean_str(request.GET.get('source_type') or request.GET.get('sourceType')).lower()
    source_id = clean_str(request.GET.get('source_id') or request.GET.get('sourceId'))
    actual = '1' if truthy(request.GET.get('actual_mappings') or request.GET.get('actualMappings')) else '0'
    key = f'ksb-coverage-response:{scope or "all"}:{clean_str(identifier)}:{source_type}:{source_id}:{actual}'
    if scope == 'programme' and request.GET.get('view') == 'summary':
        key += ':summary-v1'

    def build():
        # One targeted read scope per build. Without it every helper below
        # re-read its parent table in full -- curriculum.modules, the training
        # rows, the programme configs, the KSB profiles -- once per caller, a
        # remote round trip each. Child reads stay on the targeted
        # ``module_catalogue_id in (...)`` query exactly as they were outside a
        # scope, so the rows are the same; only the repeats go.
        with curriculum_read_scope(targeted_child_reads=True):
            response = _coverage_response_uncached(request, scope, identifier)
        return encode_json_bytes(response.content, status=response.status_code)

    part = request.GET.get('view') if scope == 'programme' else ''
    if part in COVERAGE_PART_VIEWS:
        # One of the two halves (see COVERAGE_PART_VIEWS). Both are cut in one
        # build, straight from the document it holds, and cached together: the
        # heatmap's cells and each item's mapping list are the same placements
        # filed two ways, so one database read serves both pages. The full
        # document is neither serialised nor cached on the way -- for the
        # largest programme encoding it and cutting the halves back out of it
        # took ~1.2 s of a cold build; cutting them directly takes ~0.17 s.
        def build_parts():
            with curriculum_read_scope(targeted_child_reads=True):
                result = _coverage_payload_uncached(request, scope, identifier)
            if isinstance(result, HttpResponse):
                error = encode_json_bytes(result.content, status=result.status_code)
                return {name: error for name in COVERAGE_PART_VIEWS}
            # coverage_part replaces top-level keys only, so a shallow copy each
            # keeps one half's cut out of the other's.
            return {name: encode_json_entry(coverage_part(dict(result), name)) for name in COVERAGE_PART_VIEWS}

        # Past its 60s an entry is re-checked against the one input no epoch
        # covers (standard_ksbs / ksb_profiles, see the docstring) and kept when
        # it has not moved, instead of being rebuilt every minute.
        return cached_curriculum_value(
            f'{key}:parts-v4', build_parts, ttl=60, fingerprint=component_source_inputs_fingerprint,
        )[part]
    return cached_curriculum_value(key, build, ttl=60, fingerprint=component_source_inputs_fingerprint)

def achievement_inputs_fingerprint(programme_id, cache_key):
    """Whether the learner data behind a cached Achievement read has moved.

    One round trip, one row back: every placement (the whole learners table is
    ~500 rows), and for this programme's learners -- by programme id, plus the
    ids the last build read -- their progress entries, those entries' KSB rows,
    and the KSB exclusion registry, each folded to a count and a sum of row
    hashes over every column the read depends on. Order-independent, so no sort:
    ~0.5 s on the server for the largest programme, against a rebuild that
    ships ~9 MB of progress rows. The curriculum side (components, mappings,
    required KSBs) is the programme's cache generation plus
    component_source_inputs_fingerprint. Any read failure answers a value that
    never matches, so the entry is rebuilt rather than trusted.
    """
    learner_ids = sorted(int(value) for value in (_ACHIEVEMENT_LEARNER_IDS.get(cache_key) or ()) if str(value).isdigit())
    try:
        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute(
                '''
                with scoped as (
                    select id from "Learner".learners where programme_id = %s or id = any(%s)
                ), entries as (
                    select p.id, hashtext(concat_ws('|', p.id, p.learner_id, p.kind, p.passed, p.component_ref,
                           p.component_title, p.component_type, p.module_ref, p.module_title, p.week_ref,
                           p.week_title, p.submitted_at, p.programme_ref, p.cohort_ref, p.group_ref,
                           p.deleted_at, p.ssot_updated_at)) as h
                    from "Learner".learner_progress_entries p
                    where p.learner_id in (select id from scoped)
                )
                select
                    (select count(*)::text || ':' || coalesce(sum(hashtext(concat_ws('|', l.id, l.full_name,
                            l.programme_id, l.cohort_id, l.group_id, l.programme_status, l.lifecycle_status,
                            l.updated_at))::bigint), 0) from "Learner".learners l),
                    (select count(*)::text || ':' || coalesce(sum(h::bigint), 0) from entries),
                    (select count(*)::text || ':' || coalesce(sum(hashtext(concat_ws('|', k.progress_id, k.position,
                            k.ksb_code, k.weight, k.weight_class))::bigint), 0)
                       from "Learner".learner_progress_ksbs k where k.progress_id in (select id from entries)),
                    (select count(*)::text || ':' || coalesce(sum(hashtext(concat_ws('|', x.progress_id, x.position,
                            x.ksb_code, x.status))::bigint), 0)
                       from "Learner".learner_progress_ksb_exclusions x)
                ''',
                [programme_id, learner_ids],
            )
            learner_side = tuple(cursor.fetchone())
    except DatabaseError:
        logger.warning('Could not fingerprint KSB achievement inputs for %s.', programme_id, exc_info=True)
        return ('unavailable', time.monotonic())
    return (
        learner_side,
        component_source_inputs_fingerprint(),
        int(time.time() // ACHIEVEMENT_INPUTS_MAX_AGE_SECONDS),
    )
